days.title: Back & Biceps
days.note: Pull day. Do the warm-up below, then 1–2 light sets of pulldowns before your working sets. Squeeze your shoulder blades on every rep.

items.note: Easy pace, long smooth strokes. Push with legs first, then pull with arms.
Arms out to the sides. Small circles growing bigger, 15 forward then 15 backward.
On hands and knees, round your back up, then let your belly drop and lift your chest. Move slowly with your breath.
Hold a light band at shoulder height. Pull it apart until it touches your chest, squeezing shoulder blades.
Hang from a bar with straight arms. Pull your shoulder blades down and back without bending elbows, then relax.
Think of pulling with your elbows, not your hands. Avoid: Swinging your body or pulling the bar behind your neck.
Pause for one second at your stomach on every rep. Avoid: Rocking your torso back and forth to move the weight.
Keep your neck in line with your spine. Look at the floor a metre ahead. Avoid: Rounding your lower back.
Imagine starting a lawnmower, but slow and controlled. Avoid: Twisting your torso to lift the weight.
The slow lowering does as much work as the lift. Avoid: Swinging your hips or letting elbows drift forward.
You can alternate arms if both together feels heavy. Avoid: Shrugging your shoulders as you lift.
Kneel, sit back on your heels and reach your arms long on the floor. Breathe into your back.
Reach one arm overhead and lean to the other side. Stretches lats and obliques.
Clasp your hands in front and push them away, rounding your upper back.
Forearms on a door frame, step through until you feel the chest open. Also stretches biceps.

days.title: Shoulders & Triceps
days.note: Push day for shoulders. Do 1–2 light sets of shoulder press after the warm-up. Go light on raises; form beats weight.

items.note: Light resistance, steady pace until you start to feel warm.
Arms out to the sides. Small circles growing bigger, 15 forward then 15 backward.
Roll your shoulders up, back and down slowly. Then reverse.
Hold a stick or band wide. Lift it over your head and behind you, then back. Widen your grip if it pinches.
Hold a light band at shoulder height. Pull it apart until it touches your chest, squeezing shoulder blades.
Keep your ribs down so your lower back doesn't arch. Avoid: Banging the dumbbells together or locking elbows hard.
Use a weight you can control. This one burns fast. Avoid: Swinging or lifting above shoulder height with a shrug.
Keep a soft bend in your elbows the whole time. Avoid: Leaning back to help the weight up.
Great for posture. Finish like a double-biceps pose. Avoid: Using so much weight that you lean back.
Only your forearms should move. Avoid: Elbows flaring out or leaning your whole body over the rope.
Brace your core so your back stays neutral. Avoid: Letting elbows flare wide. (Shown standing. Seated works the same way.)
Bend your knees to make it easier, straighten legs to make it harder. Avoid: Dropping too low, which strains the front of the shoulder.
Pull one arm across your chest with the other hand. Keep the shoulder down.
Reach one hand down your back and gently press the elbow with the other hand.
Forearms on a door frame, step through until you feel the chest open. Also stretches biceps.
Tilt your ear toward your shoulder and gently assist with your hand.

days.title: Chest & Abs
days.note: Chest first while you're fresh, abs to finish. Do 2 light bench sets after the warm-up. Use a spotter for heavy bench sets.

items.note: Start walking, then build to an easy jog you could talk through.
Arms out to the sides. Small circles growing bigger, 15 forward then 15 backward.
Swing your arms open wide to stretch the chest, then cross them in front. Keep it smooth.
Bend forward, walk hands out to a plank, then walk feet up to hands. Stand and repeat.
Feet planted, arms out in front. Rotate side to side from your mid-back. Shown with a ball. No ball needed.
Keep your shoulder blades pinned back the whole set. Avoid: Bouncing the bar off your chest or lifting your hips.
This hits the upper chest. Keep the incline low, not upright. Avoid: Letting the dumbbells drift toward your face.
Squeeze your chest hard for one second when hands meet. Avoid: Bending your elbows more as you push. That turns it into a press.
Do them on your knees once full reps get sloppy. Avoid: Hips sagging or sticking up.
Use the 45s button on the timer to time your hold. Avoid: Letting your hips drop or holding your breath.
Use the captain's chair station if hanging is tough on your grip. Avoid: Swinging to create momentum.
Slow and controlled works better than fast. Avoid: Pulling on your neck with your hands.
Forearms on a door frame, step through until you feel the chest open. Also stretches biceps.
Pull one arm across your chest with the other hand. Keep the shoulder down.
Lie face down, hands under shoulders. Press up gently to stretch your abs, hips stay down.
Reach one arm overhead and lean to the other side. Stretches lats and obliques.

days.title: Legs + Cardio
days.note: Biggest day of the week. Take the warm-up seriously before squatting. Finish with incline walking.

items.note: Light resistance, steady pace until you start to feel warm.
Hands on hips, draw big circles with your hips. 10 each direction.
Hold a wall. Swing one leg forward and back 10 times, then side to side 10 times. Switch legs.
Squat to a comfortable depth, chest up, heels down. Slow and controlled.
Step into a deep lunge, put the same-side elbow toward the floor, then rotate and reach that arm to the ceiling.
Push your knees out in line with your toes. Avoid: Heels lifting or knees caving inward.
Higher feet target glutes more, lower feet target quads. Avoid: Your lower back peeling off the seat at the bottom.
It's a hip hinge, not a squat. Knees barely bend. Avoid: Rounding your back to reach lower.
Do them in place if the gym floor is busy. Avoid: Front knee collapsing inward. (Shown in place. For walking lunges, step forward into each rep.)
Point your toes up toward your shins for a better squeeze. Avoid: Hips lifting off the pad.
Full range matters more than heavy weight here. Avoid: Bouncing at the bottom.
Steady cardio after legs helps recovery and burns fat. Avoid: Gripping the rails, which takes the work off your legs. (Set the incline higher than shown.)
Pull your heel toward your glute until you feel the front of the thigh stretch. Standing works too. Shown lying on the side. You can also do it standing.
Lie on your back, loop a towel around one foot and raise the straight leg until you feel a stretch. Shown with a band. A towel works.
Kneel on one knee, squeeze that glute and shift your hips forward.
Lie on your back, cross one ankle over the other knee and pull the bottom leg toward you.
Hands on a wall, one leg back with heel down. Lean in until the calf stretches.

days.title: Full Body
days.note: One big move for each part of the body. Moderate weights, crisp form. Do one light set of each lift after the warm-up.

items.note: Easy pace, long smooth strokes. Push with legs first, then pull with arms.
Arms out to the sides. Small circles growing bigger, 15 forward then 15 backward.
Bend forward, walk hands out to a plank, then walk feet up to hands. Stand and repeat.
Step into a deep lunge, put the same-side elbow toward the floor, then rotate and reach that arm to the ceiling.
Squat to a comfortable depth, chest up, heels down. Slow and controlled.
Keep the bar touching your legs the whole way up. Avoid: Rounding your back or jerking the bar off the floor.
A great squat to learn depth and posture. Avoid: Leaning forward and letting the dumbbell drop away from your chest.
Dumbbells let each arm work evenly. Avoid: Elbows flared straight out at 90°.
Use the assisted machine or a band to hit the rep range. Avoid: Kicking or half reps.
Finish with the weight stacked over your mid-foot. Avoid: Leaning back hard to push the weight up.
Builds grip strength that helps your deadlifts and rows. Avoid: Letting your shoulders round forward.
Kneel, sit back on your heels and reach your arms long on the floor. Breathe into your back.
Lie on your back, loop a towel around one foot and raise the straight leg until you feel a stretch. Shown with a band. A towel works.
Forearms on a door frame, step through until you feel the chest open. Also stretches biceps.
Pull your heel toward your glute until you feel the front of the thigh stretch. Standing works too. Shown lying on the side. You can also do it standing.
Lie on your back, cross one ankle over the other knee and pull the bottom leg toward you.

days.title: Full Body Cardio
days.note: Circuit: do all six back-to-back, 40 seconds work and 20 seconds rest each. Rest 2 minutes after the circuit. Repeat for 4 rounds. Each set button is one round.

items.note: Start walking, then build to an easy jog you could talk through.
Hands on hips, draw big circles with your hips. 10 each direction.
Arms out to the sides. Small circles growing bigger, 15 forward then 15 backward.
Hold a wall. Swing one leg forward and back 10 times, then side to side 10 times. Switch legs.
Bend forward, walk hands out to a plank, then walk feet up to hands. Stand and repeat.
Step side to side instead of jumping to make it low-impact. Avoid: Landing heavily on your heels. (Shown as a star jump. For jumping jacks, land with feet together each rep.)
Skip the jump and step back if you're getting sloppy. Avoid: Letting your hips sag in the plank.
Slow it down to make it a core exercise; speed it up for cardio. Avoid: Hips bouncing high in the air.
Power comes from your hips, not your arms. Avoid: Squatting it up or lifting with your shoulders. (Shown one-handed. Use both hands on the handle.)
Do regular fast squats if your knees don't like jumping. Avoid: Landing with straight, stiff legs.
No rope? Mime it. The footwork is what counts. Avoid: Jumping too high or swinging your whole arms.
Slow walk to bring your heart rate down. Breathe deeply.
Straight leg in front, pull your toes toward you and hinge forward. Shown with a band. A towel works.
Pull your heel toward your glute until you feel the front of the thigh stretch. Standing works too. Shown lying on the side. You can also do it standing.
Kneel, sit back on your heels and reach your arms long on the floor. Breathe into your back.

days.title: Rest & Recover
days.note: No gym today. Muscles grow while you recover. Sleep 7–9 hours, drink plenty of water, and do some light movement.

items.note: Gentle movement helps sore muscles recover faster. Avoid: Turning it into a hard workout. (Walk outdoors or on a flat treadmill.)
Great after a week of squats and sitting at a desk. Avoid: Arching your lower back.
Undoes the tightness from bench days. Avoid: Forcing it into pain. (A doorway frame gives the same stretch.)
Slow rolling works better than fast. Avoid: Rolling directly on your lower back or joints. (Shown on the quads. Repeat on back, hamstrings and calves.)
